routes.label: Compare groups of the same size

question: Suppose that \(S\) is a finite set of positive integers. If the greatest integer in \(S\) is removed from \(S,\) then the average value (arithmetic mean) of the integers remaining is \(32.\) If the least integer in \(S\) is also removed, then the average value of the integers remaining is \(35.\) If the greatest integer is then returned to the set, the average value of the integers rises to \(40.\) The greatest integer in the original set \(S\) is \(72\) greater than the least integer in \(S.\) What is the average value of all the integers in the set \(S?\)
solution:
The groups with means \(32\) and \(40\) have the same number of integers, so comparing their totals will reveal the size of the set.

Starting with the group that omits the greatest integer, replace the least integer with the greatest. This produces the group that omits the least integer. The total increases by \(72\), while the mean increases by \(40-32=8\). Therefore each group contains
\[
\frac{72}{8}=9
\]
integers, and the original set contains \(10\).

Removing both extremes leaves eight integers with mean \(35\), so their total is
\[
8\cdot35=280.
\]
The nine integers remaining after only the greatest is removed have total \(9\cdot32=288\). These consist of the eight middle integers and the least integer, so the least integer is
\[
288-280=8.
\]
The group omitting only the least integer has total \(9\cdot40=360\). Returning the least integer gives the original total \(360+8=368\).

Thus the requested average is
\[
\frac{368}{10}=\boxed{36.8},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
